content: An article from News roundup Lilly, Hims reach GLP-1 deal; Alnylam sales chief to step down The deal is part of a course change for Hims, which had previously sold knockoff GLP-1 drugs. Elsewhere, a medicine Servier recently acquired failed a key trial and Ultragenyx announced staff cuts. Published Nov. 6, 2026 By BioPharma Dive staff Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Getty Images Today, a brief rundown of news involving Eli Lilly and Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, as well as updates from Servier, Ultragenyx, Boehringer Ingelheim and ANI Pharmaceuticals that you may have missed. Eli Lilly will offer its obesity drugs Zepbound and Foundayo on Hims & Hers’ telehealth platform, the companies announced Friday. Under the deal, eligible patients with a prescription can use Hims to gain access to Lilly’s drugs at the same “self-pay” prices available elsewhere. Foundayo carries an initial $149 monthly price tag, while Zepbound starts at $299 per month. Hims had previously used legal loopholes to make lower-cost, compounded versions of GLP-1 weight loss drugs. But it changed course in March after a legal challenge from Novo, adopting a new strategy based on providing U.S. consumers access to an array of FDA-approved weight loss medicines. title: Karyopharm Enters Chapter 11 in Planned Merger With Ayrmid
content: Advertisement News|Articles|November 3, 2026 Karyopharm Enters Chapter 11 in Planned Merger With Ayrmid Author(s)Pharmaceutical Executive Editorial Staff Karyopharm filed for Chapter 11 under a plan to merge with Ayrmid, with competing bids allowed and closing targeted for the first quarter of 2027. Advertisement Karyopharm Therapeutics, the maker of the multiple myeloma treatment Xpovio (selinexor), filed for Chapter 11 protection on Nov. 2 under a restructuring support agreement that provides for a merger with Ayrmid, the parent company of Gamida Cell.1 The plan would convert roughly $276 million of funded debt into a majority stake in the combined company and cancel existing common and preferred shares without a distribution.2The company will seek court approval of bidding procedures that allow other parties to submit competing offers, with closing expected in the first quarter of 2027.1 “Following a comprehensive review of available alternatives, we believe this process provides a clear framework to pursue a value maximizing transaction for our stakeholders while continuing our important work of advancing therapies for patients with multiple myeloma and myelofibrosis,” said Richard Paulson, president and CEO of Karyopharm.1Key FactsDeal: Ayrmid merger through Chapter 11 planLead bidder: Ayrmid; rival bids allowedDebtor-in-possession financing: up to $55MDebt holders to receive 55% of combined companyExisting shareholders: no distributionProduct: Xpovio (selinexor), exportin 1 inhibitorTarget close: first quarter of 2027“We see considerable potential in Karyopharm’s marketed products, development pipeline and experienced team, and believe that, together, we can build a broader, stronger commercial-stage hematology business with meaningful opportunities for future growth.” — Dr. Joe Wiley, chairman and chief executive officer of AyrmidWhat are the proposed merger terms?Under the plan described in Karyopharm’s disclosure statement, which the court has not yet approved, creditors holding the roughly $276 million of funded debt would receive 55% of the combined company’s common stock, along with contingent value rights tied to future Xpovio sales in myelofibrosis.2 Ayrmid’s existing equity holders would receive the remaining 45% and contingent equity tied to future revenue from its product Omisirge.2 The combined company would emerge with no more than $135 million of funded debt, a reduction of about $141 million, and Karyopharm’s common stock is expected to be delisted from Nasdaq.2Karyopharm has secured commitments for up to $55 million in debtor-in-possession financing from existing secured lenders, which, with cash from operations, is expected to support the business during the case once the court approves it.1 The company says it expects ordinary operations and partnerships to continue without disruption.1 The market test remains open: if a rival bid meets conditions that include at least $335 million in net proceeds at closing, the company may pursue a sale instead of the merger.2Why did Karyopharm file for Chapter 11?The disclosure statement attributes the filing to sustained operating losses and a reliance on capital markets that depended on clinical progress.2 When two phase 3 readouts in 2026 fell short of expectations and liquidity tightened, secured creditors agreed to payment deferrals and forbearances.2 A formal sale process launched in July 2026 drew multiple proposals, none of which was actionable before the company exhausted its liquidity, according to the filing.2 Ayrmid’s proposal emerged from that process.2 (()=>{var l=(n,t)=>{let i=async()=>{await(await n())()},e=typeof show?Xpovio is an oral exportin 1 inhibitor that Karyopharm markets in the United States for adults with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma.1 In the randomized, open-label phase 3 BOSTON trial of 402 previously treated patients, once-weekly selinexor with bortezomib and dexamethasone produced median progression-free survival of 13.93 months, compared with 9.46 months for twice-weekly bortezomib and dexamethasone (hazard ratio, 0.70).3 Grade 3 or 4 thrombocytopenia occurred in 39% of patients receiving selinexor and 17% in the control arm.3 Myelofibrosis is the company’s other stated priority. In the phase 3 SENTRY trial of 353 patients, 50% of those given selinexor plus ruxolitinib reached a spleen volume reduction of at least 35% at week 24, versus 28% with ruxolitinib alone, but the groups did not differ significantly on the symptom-score co-primary endpoint, according to company-reported topline results.4 Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 70% of patients on the combination and 50% on ruxolitinib alone.4 Karyopharm submitted a supplemental new drug application seeking accelerated approval on Aug. 31, 2026.2How does the merger fit hematology commercial strategy?Ayrmid markets two FDA-approved products in the United States: Omisirge (omidubicel-onlv), a cell therapy for certain hematologic malignancies and severe aplastic anemia, and Aphexda (motixafortide), which mobilizes hematopoietic stem cells in adults with multiple myeloma.1 Multiple myeloma is the point at which the two companies’ marketed products overlap. “We see a strong strategic fit between Ayrmid and Karyopharm, with complementary portfolios, established commercial capabilities and a shared commitment to addressing significant unmet needs in hematology,” said Dr. Joe Wiley, chairman and chief executive officer of Ayrmid.1What risks and open questions remain?The plan still requires court confirmation. Holders of all claims entitled to vote have agreed to support it, according to the filing, so uncertainty centers on court approval, rival bids and regulatory reviews.2 Creditor voting closes Nov. 30, and the company has asked for a hearing on Jan. 11, 2027.2 Antitrust and foreign investment reviews are under evaluation, while FDA approval of the transaction itself is not expected to be required.2Projections for the combined company will be filed later with a plan supplement, so the commercial case remains unquantified.2 No FDA decision on the myelofibrosis application is reported in the sources reviewed, and SENTRY’s mixed result leaves that program’s regulatory outcome unsettled.2SourcesKaryopharm Therapeutics Inc. announces planned merger with Ayrmid Ltd. to strengthen company for the future. title: STAT Plus: Coming readout of Kymera eczema trial is a high-stakes moment in a bid to rival Dupixent
content: STAT PlusBiotech Coming readout of Kymera eczema trial is a high-stakes moment in a bid to rival Dupixent Biotech aspires to turn pill into a therapy for multiple immunology and inflammatory disorders Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Adobe By Jonathan WosenNov. 2, 2026 West Coast Biotech & Life Sciences Reporter Jonathan Wosen[email protected]Jonathan Wosen is STAT’s West Coast biotech & life sciences reporter. You can reach Jonathan on Signal at jwosen.27. Over the past decade, Sanofi and Regeneron’s Dupixent has become the top-selling drug in immunology, bringing in tens of billions in revenue while transforming outcomes for the 1.4 million patients currently on the therapy for conditions including eczema, asthma, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. But investors and doctors are intensely following an experimental therapy positioned to rival the pharma blockbuster, with results from a key study fast approaching. Massachusetts biotech Kymera Therapeutics plans to announce data from a mid-stage clinical trial of its lead asset, KT-621, in eczema before the end of the year. Market analysts for the investment bank Jefferies, using common shorthand for immunology and inflammatory disorders, have called the upcoming results “one of the most impactful I&I readouts this year.” Advertisement Success (or failure) could have major consequences for Kymera, its growing list of competitors, and the millions of people who live with eczema in the United States. The results could also bolster or dampen the biotech’s aspirations to treat a broader class of immunological diseases with its drug, including chronic spontaneous urticaria and asthma. Analysts forecast that the drug’s sales could reach nearly $4 billion by 2035, including more than $3 billion in eczema revenue, according to Visible Alpha. content: An article from Dive Brief Genmab soars to record highs after cancer drug succeeds in key trial The latest data adds to a streak of readouts that could position the company to surpass $10 billion in total annual revenue in the years ahead, according to analysts. Published Oct. 29, 2026 Delilah Alvarado Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Courtesy of Genmab A/S Dive Brief: An experimental drug that Genmab gained in an $8 billion buyout succeeded in a late-stage trial in a form of head and neck cancer, sending shares of the Danish drugmaker soaring to an all-time high. At an early analysis, a combination of Genmab’s drug petosemtamab and the immunotherapy Keytruda, cut the risk of death by half compared to Keytruda alone when used as a first-line treatment in people whose head and neck squamous cell carcinoma is positive for the protein PD-L1. The regimen met dual main objectives on response rates and survival. The latest finding represents the third consecutive positive late-stage readout in a few weeks for Genmab, providing an important boost ahead of the patent expiry for the multiple myeloma drug Darzalex. The company will share detailed results with global regulatory authorities and present them at a future medical meeting. Though Johnson & Johnson owns commercial rights to Darzalex, Genmab derives royalties that heavily contributed to the roughly $3.7 billion in revenue the company booked in 2025. Genmab inherited petosemtamab when it acquired the Dutch biotechnology company Merus last year. The drug — a bispecific antibody targeting the proteins EGFR and LGR5 — had already produced positive results in a Phase 2 trial. Genmab predicted the antibody could become a blockbuster by 2029, should those results be replicated in a late-stage study. Ahead of those findings, Genmab scored two other wins that have lifted its revenue potential. Earlier this month, the company and partner AbbVie announced the blood cancer drug Epkinly succeeded in a Phase 3 trial in frontline lymphoma. Wall Street analysts claimed the results have positioned Epkinly to become a new treatment standard in people with newly diagnosed, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The company continued its streak last week when an antibody-drug conjugate dubbed rinatabart sesutecan hit its goal in a late-stage study in ovarian cancer. Genmab picked up that therapy in a 2024 buyout of startup ProfoundBio. Wednesday’s result positions petosemtamab to become part of a new treatment standard in first-line head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, wrote TD Cowen analyst Yaron Werber. The findings should support a “broad” label enabling access regardless of whether patients’ tumors are driven by HPV infections, he wrote. The trio of successes show Genmab has “delivered on the late-stage catalysts that define the company’s longer-term growth story,” wrote William Blair analyst Matt Phipps, in a Thursday client note. The company is now on the path to surpassing $10 billion in annual revenue, with pending launches that can “more than offset the impending loss of Darzalex royalties,” Phipps added. Petosemtamab is being tested in multiple other Phase 3 trials, among them studies in second- and third-line recurrent head and neck cancer, and a trial in colorectal cancer. Kemny/Science Photo Library By Elaine ChenOct. 27, 2026 National Biotech Reporter Elaine Chen[email protected]Elaine’s stories explore the boom in new obesity treatments, new drug payment models, the ways companies are affected by FDA changes, and the emerging psychedelics drug sector. She co-writes The Readout newsletter, and co-hosts STAT’s weekly biotech podcast, The Readout Loud. You can reach Elaine on Signal at elaineywchen.70. Artiva Biotherapeutics said Tuesday that it’s winding down after two patients died in a trial testing its cell therapy for autoimmune diseases, the latest in a series of safety events that have emerged in a promising research field. One participant in the Phase 2 study died from a neurological complication after receiving the treatment, an NK cell therapy. Researchers determined the death was likely not related to the cell therapy itself, but to a chemotherapy that was given before the cell therapy, Artiva said. It’s standard to give patients chemotherapies before infusing cell therapies to lower the patients’ white blood cell count and make room for the new cells.Advertisement Related Story STAT Plus: Patient dies in Bristol Myers Squibb autoimmune CAR-T trial A second participant experienced sudden death about two months after treatment. Researchers determined that this was not related to any component of the treatment process, but the cause of death has not been determined, the San Diego-based company said. Journavx, notably, was dinged by one-time rebate accounting, so the “softer” quarter shouldn’t raise major concerns about the product, according to RBC Capital Markets analyst Brian Abrahams. In a note to clients, Abrahams wrote that the “solid” performance from Vertex’s cystic fibrosis drugs “underscores one of the steadiest, high-margin, and likely most durable core large biopharma franchises.” Vertex slightly upped its annual revenue guidance on Monday afternoon, to a range of $13.15 billion to $13.25 billion. Company shares, meanwhile, were down about 3% by mid-morning Tuesday. In his own note, David Risinger of Leerink Partners pointed out that Vertex’s earnings per share this quarter were 4% below consensus. The operating and financing costs associated with Crinetics — an endocrine drug developer that Vertex just purchased for $10 billion — also put pressure on near-term earnings. One of the bigger pieces of “good news,” according to Risinger and others, is that company leaders expressed confidence in their ability to launch Vertex’s first kidney product. But being marked as an important growth driver has also put a magnifying glass on the potential obstacles to pove’s commercial prospects. For example, a citizen’s petition filed in late October asked the FDA to, for safety reasons, require regular monitoring of antibody levels for patients taking the drug, as well as guidance for managing low levels. Two similar medicines are already available, too. Additionally, Vertex wants to provide pove as a highly concentrated, low volume shot delivered about once a month via an at-home autoinjector. Developing and scaling the manufacturing for that kind of product is often challenging. Still, Vertex executives affirmed their conviction. With the FDA’s decision deadline fast-approaching, “we are 100% ready” to sell the product and “are incredibly excited to bring pove to patients,” McKechnie said. The company “essentially gave bulls what they wanted to hear,” wrote Carter Gould, an analyst at Cantor Fitzgerald, in a note to clients. “Given that this was arguably one of the last opportunities to potentially reset expectations around approval or the label ahead of the [decision deadline], management's repeated expressions of confidence should be viewed as strongly encouraging,” Gould added. Earlier this year, when Vertex reported key late-stage data for pove, Gould described the results as “the first major step” to unlocking a renal franchise that could exceed $10 billion in peak annual sales. Such a franchise would go “a long way toward differentiating Vertex’s growth profile [versus its] larger-cap peers.” Another core piece of that franchise is inaxaplin, which is in testing as a treatment for kidney disease caused by mutations in a gene called APOL1. title: Your Questions Answered: Foundayo’s EU Panel Backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s Masked TCE Bet, FDA’s Rare Disease Overhaul, and More
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 19, 2026 Your Questions Answered: Foundayo’s EU Panel Backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s Masked TCE Bet, FDA’s Rare Disease Overhaul, and More Foundayo’s EU backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s masked TCE deal, FDA’s rare disease reset, and Bausch + Lomb’s new interim CEO — explained. Advertisement Lilly’s Foundayo Receives Positive CHMP Opinion for EuropeWhat did the EMA committee recommend?The European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use recommended granting marketing authorization in the EU for Foundayo (orforglipron) for two indications: weight management in adults with obesity or overweight, and the treatment of type 2 diabetes in adults whose blood glucose is not adequately controlled. The European Commission makes the final approval decision and typically follows CHMP recommendations within a few weeks.What is Foundayo and why does it matter?Foundayo is Eli Lilly’s oral GLP-1 receptor agonist — a once-daily pill that can be taken at any time of day without food and water restrictions. That last point distinguishes it from other oral GLP-1 therapies currently on the market. The drug received FDA approval for obesity in April 2026 and launched commercially in the United States in the second quarter. Lilly has submitted orforglipron for regulatory review in approximately 40 markets globally.The Stories Covered in this PieceEMA Panel Backs Lilly’s Foundayo for Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes in EuropeFDA Approves Enspryng (Satralizumab) for Thyroid Eye DiseaseAstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 BillionFDA Launches Rare Disease Framework InitiativeVir Biotechnology Enters R&D Collaboration with Gilead for Three Novel PRO-XTEN Dual Masked T-Cell EngagersBausch + Lomb Appoints Thomas Appio as Interim CEOWhat does this mean competitively?If the European Commission approves Foundayo, it would become the second oral GLP-1 available in the EU for weight management, following Novo Nordisk’s Wegovy pill, which received European approval in July for weight management only. In the type 2 diabetes setting, Foundayo would compete with Novo’s Rybelsus brand of oral semaglutide, which has been on the European market since 2020 and has grown into a multi-billion-dollar franchise. The CHMP recommendation opens a new competitive front between Lilly and Novo Nordisk in Europe’s oral GLP-1 market, adding to their existing rivalry in injectable incretin therapies.What did the clinical evidence show?The weight management recommendation is based on two studies involving more than 4,740 adults with obesity or overweight. The type 2 diabetes recommendation is based on four studies involving 3,765 adults compared against placebo, dapagliflozin, and oral semaglutide.FDA Approves Enspryng for Thyroid Eye DiseaseWhat was approved?The FDA approved Enspryng (satralizumab), an interleukin-6 receptor inhibitor developed by Roche, for adults with thyroid eye disease on October 16. Roche describes it as the first subcutaneous therapy for the condition — one that patients or caregivers can administer at home after training from a healthcare provider. It is Enspryng’s second indication; the drug was first approved in 2020 for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.What did the clinical trials show?The approval rests on two identically designed Phase 3 trials, SatraGO-1 and SatraGO-2, which enrolled 258 adults across 19 countries. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients with active, moderate-to-severe disease who achieved at least a 2 mm reduction in proptosis — eye bulging — at week 24. Results diverged: SatraGO-2 met its endpoint, with 52.9% of Enspryng-treated patients achieving a proptosis response versus 23.4% on placebo, and 60.7% showing reduced double vision versus 25.8%. SatraGO-1 did not reach statistical significance, with researchers attributing the gap to an unexpectedly high placebo response.How does this change the treatment landscape?Two disease-specific therapies were already approved — Tepezza and, more recently, Lumvoa — both administered by intravenous infusion. Enspryng’s subcutaneous, every-four-week maintenance dosing offers a different treatment experience, with the key benefit being reduced logistical burden rather than a demonstrated efficacy advantage over existing options. No head-to-head comparison with approved therapies was conducted.What are the remaining unknowns?Roche did not disclose pricing or launch timing. Long-term data beyond week 24 were not described in available sources. Separately, the FDA has granted priority review to a supplemental Enspryng application for myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease, with a decision expected in January 2027. Insitro will receive $40 million upfront and is eligible for up to approximately $1.46 billion in development and commercial milestones, plus single-digit royalties on global sales.What is insitro’s platform?Insitro’s Virtual Human platform combines large-scale human and cellular data with AI-enabled target identification and medicine design. The company was founded in 2018 and reports more than $750 million in capital raised, with existing collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb, Lilly and Gilead. It has nine programs in development, including genetic regulators of liver fat and fibrosis expected to enter the clinic in early 2027.Why MASH and cardiomyopathies?Both conditions are characterized by disease heterogeneity — a single diagnostic label covering patients whose underlying biology differs — which has complicated treatment development. In MASH, the FDA approved its first treatment, resmetirom (Rezdiffra), in March 2024, but the condition still lacks therapeutic options for most of the estimated 6 to 8 million US patients with moderate-to-advanced liver scarring. The cardiomyopathy scope was not specified in the announcement.What are the limitations of this deal?No drug candidates were named in the announcement. The collaboration sits at the discovery stage, with targets identified through AI-driven analysis still requiring validation through preclinical and clinical work. The $40 million upfront represents less than 3% of the total headline value, and neither company disclosed timelines for milestone payments.FDA Launches Rare Disease Framework InitiativeWhat is the Rare Disease Framework Initiative?The FDA announced a new effort to redesign how drugs and biologics for rare diseases are developed and reviewed. The initiative, outlined in a white paper released by the agency’s Rare Disease Innovation Hub, aims to build a regulatory framework tailored to the realities of small patient populations — covering clinical development, evidence standards, manufacturing review, and the role of patient voice throughout the process.Why is FDA doing this now?Despite years of regulatory flexibility programs for rare diseases, only approximately 5% of rare conditions currently have an FDA-approved treatment. The agency says that gap reflects the need for a more fundamentally tailored approach rather than incremental adjustments to a framework originally designed for common diseases.What are the specific commitments?The initiative outlines six priority areas: greater clarity and predictability in regulatory decision-making through tailored guidance; embedding the patient voice early and at defined milestones; leveraging external expertise for customized review; building shared institutional knowledge; applying risk-based approaches to manufacturing and pre-approval inspections; and championing innovative statistical approaches in rare disease development.What happens next?The FDA is hosting a public meeting on October 28 at its White Oak campus, facilitated by the Reagan-Udall Foundation, to gather input from patients, disease advocates, industry, and other stakeholders. Additional sector-specific roundtables and requests for information will follow. The detailed framework development — which could include new guidance, regulatory changes, and organizational changes within FDA — will be informed by that input.Gilead and Vir Biotechnology Enter $1.87 Billion Masked T-Cell Engager CollaborationWhat are the two companies agreeing to develop?Vir Biotechnology will discover and optimize three novel PRO-XTEN dual-masked T-cell engager development candidates for Gilead, targeting selected solid tumor-associated antigens. Gilead holds an exclusive license to develop, manufacture and commercialize the resulting therapies. Vir will receive $90 million upfront — including $65 million in cash and a $25 million equity investment at a 30% premium — and is eligible for up to $1.74 billion in additional milestones and tiered royalties.What is the PRO-XTEN masking technology?PRO-XTEN is designed to keep T-cell engagers inactive in circulation until they reach the tumor microenvironment, where tumor-specific proteases cleave the mask and activate the drug’s cancer-killing mechanism. That conditional activation is intended to limit systemic toxicity — one of the primary barriers to TCE use in solid tumors — while extending the drug’s half-life and potentially enabling less frequent dosing.Why does this matter for solid tumor oncology?T-cell engagers have proven highly effective in blood cancers but have faced significant limitations in solid tumors, where toxicity and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment have constrained clinical use. Vir’s PRO-XTEN approach directly targets those barriers. This is the second major PRO-XTEN collaboration — an earlier $1.7 billion deal with Astellas for a PSMA-targeted TCE in prostate cancer was announced in February 2026. Together the two deals bring total PRO-XTEN platform value to more than $3.6 billion across two top-tier pharma partners.How does this fit Gilead’s oncology strategy?Today’s deal is Gilead’s third major solid tumor oncology transaction in 2026, following the $5 billion Tubulis ADC acquisition in April and the $2.1 billion Ouro Medicines BCMA T-cell engager acquisition in March. Gilead is simultaneously building in ADCs, T-cell engagers for autoimmune disease, and now masked T-cell engagers for solid tumors — a deliberate multi-mechanism oncology buildout executed across a single year.Bausch + Lomb Appoints Thomas Appio as Interim CEOWhat happened at Bausch + Lomb?Bausch + Lomb announced that Brent Saunders departed as CEO by mutual agreement, with Thomas J. Appio named interim CEO effective immediately. Appio, who will retain his role as CEO of parent company Bausch Health, steps into the position just weeks before the company reports third-quarter results and updates its full-year guidance on October 28.What does the company expect for 2026?Simultaneously with the leadership announcement, both Bausch + Lomb and Bausch Health said they expect to raise their full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance based on preliminary third-quarter results, citing strong business performance and anticipated momentum through year-end.What was Saunders building?Saunders returned to Bausch + Lomb in March 2023 — his second stint as CEO — and spent three years stabilizing the company’s supply chain, accelerating commercial execution, and rebuilding its R&D pipeline. In the latest draft guidance, regulators focused on treatments designed to correct different mutations in the same disease-causing gene. Often, the individual mutations are so rare that traditional clinical trials are impractical or even impossible. Under the plan, a drugmaker could win approval for a specific personalized gene therapy targeting one mutation using more of a traditional approach, then later win clearance for different mutations with laboratory data instead of a whole new clinical study. Prime shares jumped 15% early Wednesday. The idea is part of a larger effort by the FDA to encourage drugmakers to develop treatments for rare diseases. Agency officials also attended a rare disease summit in Washington this week. “Senior policymakers are clearly supportive of rare disease,” RBC Capital Markets analyst Luca Issi wrote in a note to clients about the summit. Issi sees a contrast with the “darker days” when former FDA officials Marty Makary and Vinay Prasad left drugmakers frustrated and confused by a series of hard-line stances on therapies even as they unveiled proposals designed to help speed products to market. As part of the administration’s rare disease efforts, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services is also looking to broaden a program that gives Medicaid patients access to cell and gene therapies. Initially, the focus was on sickle cell disease. A big question for developers of gene-editing medicines has been whether one-time prices would become a “roadblock,” Beam’s Evans wrote on X. “Or would payers work to ensure access for patients and capture the long-term benefits of eliminating lifelong medical expenses and chronic treatments?” The CMS plan to expand its access program is “great news,” he said. 舒华博（阿舒克森片）用于降低缺血性卒中或高风险短暂性脑缺血发作（TIA）成人患者的卒中风险，不包括心源性栓塞型卒中患者。拜耳舒华博（阿舒克森片）上市申请获得优先审评资格，从受理到获批历时约半年时间，在中国获得全球首批。此次批准基于全球关键性III期OCEANIC-STROKE研究的积极数据。该研究是首个成功完成并取得阳性结果的FXIa抑制剂III期卒中研究。FXIa位于内源性凝血通路的关键环节，主要参与病理性血栓的形成和扩增，而对正常生理性止血的影响相对有限。阿舒克森通过选择性抑制FXIa，旨在突破传统强化抗栓治疗中“增强疗效往往伴随出血增加”的临床困境，在现有抗血小板治疗基础上提供额外保护。（2）君赛生物首个创新药诺吉仑赛申报上市10月26日，CDE官网显示，君赛生物诺吉仑赛上市申请获得受理，用于既往接受过至少两种系统治疗（含PD-1抗体）失败的不可切除或转移性黑色素瘤患者。诺吉仑赛注射液（GC101）是依托君赛生物自主开发的DeepTIL™细胞富集扩增平台开发而成，是公司研发进度最快的TIL疗法管线，也是全球首款无需高强度清淋化疗、无需IL-2给药的TIL疗法。2026年6月，君赛生物在美国临床肿瘤学会（ASCO）年会上，以LBA口头报告形式首次公布诺吉仑赛治疗晚期黑色素瘤的关键II期研究结果。（3）智翔金泰IL-4Rα单抗拟纳入优先审评10月26日，CDE官网公示显示，智翔金泰申报的1类新药泰利奇拜单抗注射液（皮下注射）拟纳入优先审评，针对适应症为慢性自发性荨麻疹。公开资料显示，这是一款IL-4Rα抗体药物。该产品用于慢性自发性荨麻疹适应症的3期临床试验已经达到了主要终点指标。泰利奇拜单抗注射液是一款由智翔金泰自主研发的重组全人源抗IL-4Rα单克隆抗体，作用靶点为IL-4Rα。据智翔金泰此前新闻稿介绍，目前，泰利奇拜单抗注射液的研发已取得多项进展。除慢性自发性荨麻疹适应症以外，其成人季节性过敏性鼻炎适应症和成人中、重度特应性皮炎适应症以及慢性鼻窦炎伴鼻息肉适应症均处于新药上市申请审评阶段，另有多个适应症处于不同临床试验阶段。（4）住友制药宣布口服menin抑制剂获FDA突破性疗法认定10月26日，住友制药（Sumitomo Pharma）宣布，美国FDA授予在研口服menin抑制剂 enzomenib（DSP-5336）突破性疗法认定，用于治疗携带KMT2A重排的复发或难治性急性白血病患者。该药此前已获得FDA快速通道资格，此次突破性疗法认定将为其后续临床开发及监管审评提供更多支持。Enzomenib是一款口服小分子药物，通过抑制menin蛋白与赖氨酸甲基转移酶2A（KMT2A）蛋白之间的相互作用发挥抗白血病作用。Menin是一种参与调控基因表达和细胞生长的支架蛋白。在携带KMT2A重排或NPM1突变的白血病细胞中，menin相关蛋白相互作用可维持异常的致癌基因表达。Enzomenib通过阻断这一相互作用，下调白血病相关致癌基因的表达，促进白血病细胞分化，从而抑制肿瘤生长。（5）艾伯维BCMA/CD3双抗提交FDA上市申请10月27日，艾伯维（AbbVie）宣布，已向美国FDA提交靶向B细胞成熟抗原（BCMA）和CD3的双特异性抗体etentamig（ABBV-383）的BLA，寻求批准其治疗复发或难治性多发性骨髓瘤成人患者。该申请基于全球3期CERVINO研究的积极结果，研究同时达到客观缓解率和无进展生存期两项主要终点。根据此前公布的3期CERVINO研究结果，etentamig组和对照组的ORR分别为74.0%和45.7%。与对照组相比，etentamig使疾病进展或死亡风险降低60%。两项主要终点均达到统计学显著性。安全性方面，在接受单次阶梯递增剂量的患者中，细胞因子释放综合征（CRS）发生率为28.3%，均为1级或2级，未报告3级及以上事件。不过，etentamig组3级或4级感染的发生率为27.7%，仍需在后续研究和临床应用中持续关注。（6）甘李药业蛋白降解1类新药获批临床10月28日，甘李药业宣布，公司自主研发的STAT6蛋白降解靶向嵌合体（PROTAC）创新药GLR2053片已正式获得中国国家药品监督管理局（CDE）药物临床试验批准，拟用于治疗特应性皮炎，给药途径为口服。据甘李药业新闻稿介绍，STAT6靶向蛋白降解靶向嵌合体药物一端可识别并特异性地结合到目标蛋白STAT6，另外一端结合E3泛素连接酶CRBN并拉近其与STAT6靶蛋白的距离，形成STAT6-PROTAC-CRBN三元复合物，使STAT6被泛素化标记并被蛋白酶体降解。现有的临床前研究显示，GLR2053片具有较好的有效性与安全性，展现出突出的临床价值与开发前景。（7）恒瑞医药重磅ADC又一适应症申报上市10月28日，CDE官网公示，恒瑞医药瑞康曲妥珠单抗的一项新适应症上市申请获得受理。根据该药的研究进度推测，本次申报的新适应症可能为HER2阳性复发或转移性乳腺癌一线治疗。这是瑞康曲妥珠单抗在国内申报的第5项适应症上市申请。2026年8月，恒瑞宣布瑞康曲妥珠单抗在用于HER2阳性复发或转移性乳腺癌一线治疗的关键Ⅲ期临床研究（研究代号：SHR-A1811-307）预设期中分析中，达到研究的主要终点。SHR-A1811-307研究为一项多中心、随机、开放、阳性对照Ⅲ期临床试验，旨在比较瑞康曲妥珠单抗联合或不联合帕妥珠单抗 Pharma宣布，美国FDA批准白细胞介素-23（IL-23）抑制剂 Ilumya（tildrakizumab）的补充生物制品许可申请（sBLA），用于治疗活动性银屑病关节炎成人患者。此次批准基于全球3期INSPIRE-1和INSPIRE-2研究的积极结果。两项研究均为随机、双盲、安慰剂对照试验，评估Ilumya（100 content: STAT PlusPharmalot FDA OKs generic HIV prevention shot, widening access for lower-income countries The annual cost per person will be $40, comparable to daily tablets Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article A pharmacist holds a vial of the HIV prevention medicine lenacapavir in Cape Town, South Africa.Nardus Engelbrecht/AP By Ed SilvermanNov. 2, 2026 Pharmalot Columnist, Senior Writer Ed Silverman[email protected]Ed’s stories explore prescription drug pricing, affordability and access, as well issues surrounding patents, litigation, and legislation. He is also the author of the morning Pharmalittle newsletter and the afternoon Pharmalot newsletter. After months of anticipation, the Food and Drug Administration gave tentative approval to Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories to make a generic version of a groundbreaking HIV prevention medicine, a key step in widening access for dozens of low- and middle-income countries. The company, one of the world’s largest generic drugmakers, plans to start shipping the medicine next month as part of an effort propelled, in part, by several global health organizations to ensure the drug becomes available in lower-income countries as quickly as possible. The annual cost per person will be $40, comparable to daily tablets.Advertisement Known as lenacapavir, the injectable drug is widely seen as a game-changing tool for eradicating HIV because it offers virtually complete protection against contracting the virus with just one administration every six months. The brand-name version, which is known as Yetzugo in the U.S., is marketed by Gilead Sciences and was approved by the FDA last year. STAT+ Exclusive Story Already have an account?
